input: Research Carvana (carvana.com) for a hedge fund

catalysts.claim: Q4 2026 earnings: no date announced yet. The prior-year Q4 report came out after the close on Feb 18, 2026, so mid-to-late February 2027 is likely, but that is an inference. It will be the first print after management said it would stop giving quarterly and annual outlooks starting with the Q4 2026 call.

The reporting regime changes: from the Q4 2026 call Carvana stops giving financial outlooks, and in 2027 it will focus on GAAP operating income and net income rather than adjusted EBITDA. This removes a guidance anchor for the stock.

The 5.500% Senior Notes due April 15, 2027 are still listed in the Q3 2026 10-Q debt disclosures. The original issue was $600M, and 94.7% ($568.2M) was exchanged in 2023, so the stub left is probably small. The current principal was not verified.
The next Manheim Used Vehicle Value Index release is Dec 7, 2026. October 2026 was 206.8, up 2% YoY and 0.5% MoM (seasonally adjusted); unadjusted prices fell 2.3% from September.
Q4 2026 setup: management expects retail units and adjusted EBITDA to rise from Q3, and FY2026 adjusted EBITDA in the higher end of $2.7-3.0B 'as long as the environment remains stable.'

results_vs_guidance.claim: Q3 2026: 217,385 retail units (+39% YoY, a record) and revenue of $8.040B (+42%). Net income was $483M (+$220M, 6.0% margin), GAAP operating income $714M (8.9% margin), and adjusted EBITDA a record $800M (+$163M). Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 10.0% from 11.3%.

Against consensus: revenue of $8.04B beat $7.67B by 4.9%, and adjusted EBITDA of $800M beat $791.3M by 1.1%. Adjusted EPS of $0.39 missed $0.48 by 18.3%. The FY EBITDA guidance midpoint of $2.85B was below the $2.93B consensus.
Total gross profit per retail unit was $6,997, down $365 YoY. Diluted EPS was $0.39, and Q3 included a $53M loss on extinguishing the 2030 secured notes early.

Gross profit per unit by line: retail +$85 (wider retail-to-wholesale spreads), wholesale -$196, other/finance -$299 (lower customer rates against rising benchmarks). Rising benchmark rates and fuel were a combined headwind of about $200 per unit. SG&A per unit was about flat: operations +$109, overhead -$159, advertising +$45.

Adjusted EBITDA per car fell YoY for a fourth straight quarter, to about $3,680 from $4,085. The $2.7-3.0B FY2026 guidance first given on Jul 29 had a midpoint below the Street, and shares fell 14% after hours that day.

Current guidance: retail units and adjusted EBITDA up sequentially in Q4, and FY2026 adjusted EBITDA in the higher end of $2.7-3.0B. Long-term goals, which management says are not guidance, are 3M annual units and a 13.5% adjusted EBITDA margin (about a 12.5% operating margin).
Consensus EPS (24 analysts) is $1.52 for FY2026, $2.25 for 2027 (up 8% over 90 days) and $2.71 for 2028. The forward P/E fell to 26x at the Oct 28 close from 63x at the end of 2025.

event_driven.claim: On Mar 13, 2026 the board approved a 5-for-1 forward split, subject to a vote at the May 5, 2026 annual meeting, with split-adjusted trading expected from May 7, 2026. It was Carvana's first split. Share counts and prices from before May 2026 are not comparable.

Capital structure as of Oct 26, 2026: 722,713,745 Class A and 380,547,355 Class B shares outstanding. The 10-Q discloses no share repurchases; the only issuance shown is through an ATM program referenced in XBRL tags.

Franchise push: Carvana owns at least 7 Stellantis franchise dealerships, including Avon Lake, OH, after a Massachusetts store bought in March 2026. Stellantis reportedly now limits dealers to one acquisition per year, which caps how fast Carvana can roll up stores. Management called the franchise work 'very early in the game.'

Short-seller overhang: Gotham City Research (Jan 28, 2026) alleged that 2023-24 earnings were inflated by more than $1B through related parties DriveTime and Bridgecrest, and predicted a delayed 10-K and restatements. The stock fell about 14%. Carvana called the report 'inaccurate and intentionally misleading,' and JPMorgan and BTIG pushed back. The 10-K was filed Feb 18, 2026.

Morgan Stanley (Percoco) named CVNA a 'Top Pick' (Overweight, $88 target), saying the EPS miss mostly reflected a one-time debt charge. Barchart's consensus target is $82 (Moderate Buy), and the stock was still down about 15% YTD.

Needham cut its target to $100 from $120 (Buy), citing higher rates. The 24-analyst average target is $81, down from $85 a year ago and a $97 January peak. Shares were about $69, roughly 30% below the January high.
Argus reiterated Buy with a $100 target. EPS beat Argus's $0.34 estimate but missed the $0.47 consensus.

credit_signals.claim: On Aug 14, 2026 Carvana signed a $1.66B senior secured Term Loan B: SOFR+225bp, issued at 99.75, maturing Aug 14, 2033, with 0.25% quarterly amortization. It has no financial maintenance covenant and carries a 50% excess-cash-flow sweep from FY2028 that steps down with leverage. Proceeds redeemed the 9%/11%/13% cash/PIK 2030 secured notes ($1.0B on Aug 15, the rest on Aug 22).
Management says the refinancing saves about $45M a year in interest. Q3 net interest expense was $98M, down from $125M a year earlier.

Liquidity at Sep 30, 2026: cash $3,049M; committed liquidity $5,120M (including $2,071M of revolver availability); total liquidity $7,503M. Extra capacity: $1.5B super senior and $750M pari passu senior debt. Debt: long-term $4,874M, current portion $283M, short-term revolvers $71M.

Loan-sale funding: Ally's purchase agreement was raised to up to $8B of receivables through July 2027. A second purchase agreement was upsized by $500M through Jan 2028, auto-extending to Jul 2028 if not fully used. One short-term revolver was extended to Aug 2027.

Remaining unsecured notes: 5.500% due Apr 2027, 5.875% due Oct 2028, 4.875% due Sep 2029, 10.250% due May 2030, plus senior secured notes due 2031. The $300M Stellantis trade floor plan line was fully drawn at Sep 30, 2026 ($300M, up from $64M at YE2025).

Last verified issuer rating action: S&P upgraded Carvana to 'B' from 'B-' with a positive outlook on Mar 13, 2025, and flagged a possible further upgrade if leverage stayed below 5x and free operating cash flow to debt above 5%. No 2026 issuer action was found.

alternative_signals.claim: Reconditioning capacity is the binding constraint. Production topped 200,000 in Q3, but growth in cars available on the website stayed 'well below' sales growth. Garcia III: 'our rate of growth is constrained by our ability to scale the supply chain.'

Capacity and hiring: an inspection and reconditioning center at ADESA Orlando (Sanford, FL) was announced Oct 6, 2026 with about 100 jobs, following ADESA Charlotte (Sep 15, about 100 jobs) and ADESA Chicago. ADESA Kansas City is slated to be the first of 56 ADESA sites to become an auction-plus-reconditioning 'megasite.' No layoff reports were found.
The Jacksonville (Dinsmore) megasite won more approvals, including a planned 77,000 sq ft inspection and reconditioning facility.

Search/marketing scrutiny: of 327 Carvana Google Business Profiles reviewed, 143 listed non-Carvana addresses, including 77 civic or government buildings. As of Nov 9, 109 of those show 'Temporarily closed' but still link to Carvana.com with tracking codes. Carvana did not comment. This is a reputational risk; no regulator is involved so far.

Wholesale prices: the Manheim index was 206.8 in October 2026 (+2% YoY). Wholesale days' supply was 28.1, flat YoY; retail used days' supply was just under 50. Prices are stable, so depreciation is not a major tailwind or headwind.

Pricing: management chose to pass lower loan rates to customers relative to benchmarks, which cut other/finance gross profit by $299 per unit. Rate increases are passed through with a lag and only partly.

insider_and_ownership.claim: Ernest Garcia II's entity ECG II SPE II sold Citibank European covered calls on 10M Class A shares: $90 strike, exercisable only Nov 19, 2027, physically settled. To secure them it pledged 12.5M Class A units and 10M Class B shares, and Garcia II guaranteed certain obligations. He beneficially owns 212,211,585 shares (22.7%, as-converted).
The Form 4 for the covered calls shows an $8.25 per-option premium, about $82.5M in cash to Garcia II's entity. It was filed Nov 3, 2026 and does not report a 10b5-1 plan.
Daniel Gill sold 253,639 shares at an average of $71.46 (about $18.1M) on Nov 3, 2026, cutting his position 24.69% to 773,548 shares. Institutions hold 56.71%.
CFO Mark Jenkins sold 63,750 shares at $69.51-73.15 (about $4.58M) on Nov 2, 2026 after exercising options, under a 10b5-1 plan adopted Aug 5, 2024. He holds 1,135,486 shares directly.
Director Ira Platt reported selling about $2.25M of stock in the first week of November 2026.
CEO Ernest Garcia III had 7,067 shares withheld for taxes on RSU vesting at $63.04 (code F, not an open-market sale), leaving 4,709,732 direct shares.

risks.claim: Unit economics are getting thinner. Adjusted EBITDA per car fell YoY for four straight quarters (about $3,680 vs $4,085), and adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 10.0% from 11.3%. Growth may be coming at the cost of profit per car.
Rate sensitivity: benchmark rates and fuel cost about $200 per unit in Q3, and finance gross profit per unit fell $299. Needham cut its target because of higher rates.

Dependence on loan buyers: gain-on-sale needs third-party buyers, chiefly Ally's commitment of up to $8B, which runs only through July 2027. A pullback or worse pricing would hit finance gross profit and liquidity.

Related-party and governance risk: the tax receivable agreement liability to related parties is $1,645M, and DriveTime transactions are ongoing. The Gotham allegations about DriveTime and Bridgecrest have kept plaintiff-firm 'investigations' alive.

Controlling holders are monetizing. Garcia II sold $90 calls on 10M shares and pledged units, which effectively caps his upside above $90 through Nov 2027. Executives sold more than $22M in the first week of November.
Visibility gets worse: with no financial outlook from the Q4 2026 call onward, the stock will trade more on reported prints. Beta is 3.55, and the one-year range is $54.46-$97.38.

Regulatory and consumer exposure: state attorneys general regularly inquire into Carvana's reconditioning, advertising, titling and lending practices. Carvana also sent breach notices after a document with personal data was disclosed by mistake, discovered Sep 30, 2026.

output.research_view: Growth is strong (+39% units, record $800M adjusted EBITDA), but profit per car is being given back: adjusted EBITDA per unit has fallen four quarters in a row as finance gross profit absorbs higher rates. With guidance ending at the Q4 call and a GAAP focus in 2027, the stock now depends on whether reconditioning capacity (the ADESA megasites) and loan-buyer funding (Ally's $8B through July 2027) can hold per-unit margins while volume grows. Insider selling and Garcia II's $90 covered call and pledge are a near-term supply overhang. The Feb 2027 print and the rate path are the key swing factors.

Outstanding principal of the 5.500% 2027 notes and of each other note series
Securities class action docket status (class certification ruling, Courthouse News page returned 403)
